q: The 'western disturbances' which bring winter rainfall to north-western India originate over the:
e: Western disturbances are extra-tropical cyclones that originate over the Mediterranean Sea and travel eastward with the westerly winds. They bring the winter rainfall, locally called Mahawat, to north-western India, which is vital for the rabi crop.

q: Under the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), commercial banks in India are required to maintain, in the form of liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities, a prescribed percentage of their:
e: SLR is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that it must maintain in cash, gold or approved securities before it can lend. It is prescribed by the RBI as a liquidity safeguard.

q: The first Budget of independent India, presented in 1947, was presented by:
e: R. K. Shanmukham Chetty, the first Finance Minister of independent India, presented the first Budget on 26 November 1947. John Mathai and C. D. Deshmukh presented Union Budgets later.

q: The 'White Revolution' in India, which made the country one of the largest producers of milk, was brought about through the programme known as:
e: Operation Flood, launched in 1970 under Dr Verghese Kurien through the NDDB, created a national milk grid linking rural milk producers to urban consumers. It turned India into the world's largest milk producer.

q: The headquarters of the New Development Bank, established by the BRICS countries, is located at:
e: The New Development Bank was set up by the BRICS countries (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa) to finance infrastructure and development projects. Its headquarters is at Shanghai, China.

q: The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act, which provided a legal framework for export-oriented zones in India, was enacted in the year:
e: The SEZ Act was passed in 2005 and came into force in February 2006, giving a stable legal framework with tax concessions and single-window clearance for export-oriented Special Economic Zones.

q: The SI unit of force is the:
e: The newton is the SI unit of force, defined as the force that gives a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared. The dyne is the smaller CGS unit of force.

q: The SI unit of pressure is the:
e: The pascal is the SI unit of pressure, equal to a force of one newton acting uniformly over an area of one square metre. Bar, torr and atmosphere are non-SI units still used in practice.

q: Which planet of the solar system is famous for its bright and prominent system of rings?
e: Saturn is famed for its broad, bright rings made of countless ice and rock particles orbiting its equator. Although other giant planets have faint rings, Saturn's ring system is by far the most prominent.

q: The first artificial satellite of the Earth, launched in 1957, was:
e: Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957, was the first artificial satellite placed in orbit around the Earth. It marked the beginning of the space age.

q: The first human being to travel into outer space, in 1961, was:
e: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on 12 April 1961, completing one orbit of the Earth aboard the spacecraft Vostok 1 in about 108 minutes.

q: The only scientist to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911), is:
e: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 for research on radioactivity and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911 for discovering radium and polonium, making her the only person honoured in two different sciences.

q: Brass, a widely used alloy, is a combination of:
e: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, valued for its golden colour, corrosion resistance and easy workability. Copper with tin forms bronze, which is a different alloy.

q: The number of chromosomes present in each normal human body cell is:
e: A normal human body cell contains 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs, half inherited from each parent. The reproductive cells (gametes) carry only 23 chromosomes.

q: 'Mein Kampf' (My Struggle) is the autobiographical book of:
e: Mein Kampf, meaning 'My Struggle', is the autobiographical book of Adolf Hitler, written during his imprisonment in 1924 and published in 1925. It set out his political ideology and anti-Semitic views.

q: The 'Harry Potter' series of fantasy novels was written by:
e: The Harry Potter series of fantasy novels, beginning with Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone in 1997, was written by the British author J. K. Rowling.

q: World Health Day, marking the founding of the World Health Organisation, is observed every year on:
e: World Health Day is observed on 7 April every year because the World Health Organisation (WHO) was founded on 7 April 1948. Each year it highlights a priority global health theme.

q: Kargil Vijay Diwas, commemorating India's victory in the Kargil conflict of 1999, is observed every year on:
e: Kargil Vijay Diwas is observed on 26 July to mark the success of Operation Vijay in 1999, when Indian forces recaptured the heights occupied by Pakistani infiltrators in the Kargil sector.

q: The French Open tennis championship, held at Roland Garros in Paris, is played on courts of:
e: The French Open is played on outdoor clay courts at the Stade Roland Garros in Paris. Clay is the slowest playing surface, producing longer rallies than grass or hard courts.

q: The Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' is a Latin expression which means:
e: The Latin words Citius, Altius and Fortius translate as Faster, Higher and Stronger respectively. Adopted as the Olympic motto, they express the athlete's striving for excellence in the Games.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'ICMS', developed by CRIS for the management of passenger coaches, stands for:
e: ICMS, the Integrated Coach Management System developed by CRIS, computerises the movement, maintenance and utilisation of passenger coaches on Indian Railways, helping depots plan coach examinations and rake links.

q: The full form of IRSE, an organised Group 'A' service of Indian Railways, is:
e: IRSE stands for the Indian Railway Service of Engineers, the organised Group 'A' civil engineering service of Indian Railways, whose officers manage track, bridges and buildings.

q: The Auxiliary Warning System (AWS), a train protection system which warns the driver and applies the brakes if a signal is passed at danger, is provided on the suburban railway network of:
e: The Auxiliary Warning System, which cautions the motorman and applies the brakes if a signal is passed at danger, is provided on the Mumbai suburban network of the Western and Central Railways.

q: In the 25 kV AC traction system of Indian Railways, a 'neutral section' is provided in the overhead equipment primarily in order to:

options.A: Step up the supply voltage for long sections
options.B: Provide an earthing point for the overhead equipment
options.C: Mark the end of a block section for the driver
options.D: Electrically separate two adjoining sections fed from different substations and phases, so that the pantograph does not bridge them

e: A neutral section is a short length of dead (unenergised) overhead equipment between two sections fed from different substations or phases. It prevents the pantograph from bridging and short-circuiting two different phases as the train passes.

q: Rail joints on Indian Railways are most commonly welded at site (in the field) by which of the following processes?
e: Alumino-thermic (Thermit) welding, based on the highly exothermic reaction of aluminium with iron oxide, is the standard process for welding rail joints at site. Flash butt welding is mainly done in plants for long welded rails.

q: On concrete sleepers laid on Indian Railways, the rails are fastened to the sleepers most commonly by means of:
e: Rails on concrete sleepers are held by elastic rail clips, which grip the rail foot with a constant toe load. This elastic fastening keeps the gauge secure while allowing slight rail movement.

q: In railway signalling on Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'RRI' stands for:
e: RRI stands for Route Relay Interlocking, a signalling system in which pressing route buttons sets points and signals through relay circuits, clearing the whole route for a train at one operation.

q: The longest tunnel on the Konkan Railway line is the:
e: The Karbude Tunnel, about 6.5 km long, is the longest tunnel on the Konkan Railway route. It was a major engineering challenge in the Western Ghats section of the line.

q: The Railway Board of India was constituted under the provisions of the:
e: The Railway Board was set up in 1905 under the Indian Railway Board Act, 1905, on the recommendation of the Robertson Committee, to manage the railways on commercial principles under the Government of India.

q: The world speed record for a steam locomotive, about 126 miles per hour set in 1938 and still unbroken, is held by the British locomotive named:
e: The British LNER locomotive Mallard reached about 126 mph on 3 July 1938, setting a world speed record for steam locomotives that remains unbroken to this day.

q: The famous British steam locomotive 'Flying Scotsman' is celebrated as the first steam locomotive to officially attain a speed of:
e: Flying Scotsman, the famous LNER express locomotive, was the first steam locomotive officially recorded at 100 miles per hour, a feat it achieved in 1934 with a dynamometer car.

q: The world's first high-speed Shinkansen line, opened in 1964 in Japan, connected Tokyo with:
e: Japan's Tokaido Shinkansen, opened in October 1964 ahead of the Tokyo Olympics, was the world's first high-speed railway line, connecting Tokyo with Osaka (Shin-Osaka station).

q: The first railway line in Germany, opened in 1835 and worked by the locomotive 'Der Adler', ran between Nuremberg and:
e: Germany's first railway, the Ludwig Railway opened in December 1835, ran between Nuremberg and Furth. It was worked by the locomotive Der Adler, built in England by Stephenson's firm.

q: Canada's first transcontinental railway, the Canadian Pacific Railway, was completed in 1885 when the ceremonial 'Last Spike' was driven at:
e: The Canadian Pacific Railway was completed on 7 November 1885 when the ceremonial Last Spike was driven at Craigellachie in British Columbia, linking eastern Canada with the Pacific coast.

q: Australia's famous long-distance train 'The Ghan', running between Adelaide and Darwin, takes its name from:

options.A: An Aboriginal word for the desert wind
options.B: A town in South Australia on its route
options.C: The Afghan cameleers who pioneered transport in the Australian outback
options.D: The first locomotive driver of the train

e: The Ghan is named after the Afghan cameleers who, in the 19th and early 20th centuries, pioneered transport across Australia's desert interior using camel trains before the railway was built.

q: The power of the President of India to promulgate an Ordinance when Parliament is not in session is conferred by which Article of the Constitution?
e: Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate an Ordinance when both Houses of Parliament are not in session and immediate action is necessary. Article 213 gives the corresponding power to State Governors.

q: All revenues received and loans raised by the Government of India are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India, which is provided for under which Article of the Constitution?
e: Article 266 provides for the Consolidated Fund of India, into which all revenues received, loans raised and moneys received in repayment of loans by the Government of India are credited.

q: Under the Constitution of India, the Parliament consists of:

options.A: The Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha only
options.B: The Prime Minister and the two Houses of Parliament
options.C: The President and the two Houses of Parliament
options.D: The Vice-President and the two Houses of Parliament

e: Under Article 79, Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses - the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People). The President is an integral part of Parliament.

q: The Ramakrishna Mission, founded in 1897 for social service and the propagation of spiritual values, was established by:
e: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission at Kolkata in 1897 in the name of his guru, Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, for social service, education and the spread of spiritual values.

q: Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, was born at:
e: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini, in present-day Nepal, as Prince Siddhartha. He attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, gave his first sermon at Sarnath and passed away at Kushinagar.

q: The Ryotwari system of land revenue settlement in British India was introduced by:
e: The Ryotwari system, under which revenue was settled directly with the cultivator (ryot), was introduced by Thomas Munro in the Madras Presidency around 1820. Lord Cornwallis is associated with the Permanent Settlement.

q: The largest island in the world is:
e: Greenland, with an area of about 2.16 million sq km, is the largest island in the world. Australia is larger but is classified as a continent, not an island.

q: The Mariana Trench, which contains the deepest known point in the world's oceans, is located in the:
e: The Mariana Trench lies in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Mariana Islands. Its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, is about 10,900 metres below sea level.

q: The New Economic Policy introduced in India in 1991 is broadly associated with:

options.D: Import Substitution and Ban on Foreign Investment

e: The New Economic Policy of 1991, introduced to meet the balance-of-payments crisis, rested on Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation - reducing industrial licensing, opening sectors to private and foreign investment, and integrating with the world economy.

q: The Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), an international reserve asset popularly known as 'paper gold', are issued by the:
e: Special Drawing Rights are an international reserve asset created and issued by the International Monetary Fund in 1969 to supplement member countries' reserves. Because they exist only as book entries, they are called 'paper gold'.

q: The SI unit of temperature is the:
e: The kelvin is the SI base unit of temperature, measured on the absolute scale that begins at absolute zero. Celsius is a derived scale commonly used in daily life.

q: The most abundant element in the universe is:
e: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, making up roughly three-fourths of its normal matter, followed by helium. It is the lightest element and the main fuel of stars.

q: The television, in its early mechanical form, was first demonstrated by the Scottish inventor:
e: Scottish inventor John Logie Baird gave the first public demonstration of a working mechanical television system in 1926, transmitting moving images using a spinning disc arrangement.

q: 'The Diary of a Young Girl', a moving account of life in hiding during the Second World War, was written by:
e: Anne Frank, a Jewish girl who hid with her family in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation, recorded her experiences in a diary. Published after the war as The Diary of a Young Girl, it became a world classic.

q: The marathon race in athletics is run over a distance of approximately:
e: The marathon is run over 42.195 kilometres (about 42 km, or 26 miles 385 yards). The distance was standardised at the 1908 London Olympics and formally adopted in 1921.

q: The headquarters of IRCON International Limited is located at:
e: IRCON International Limited, the railway construction PSU under the Ministry of Railways, has its registered and corporate office in New Delhi.

q: The headquarters of RITES Limited is located at:
e: RITES Limited, the transport consultancy and engineering PSU, is headquartered at Gurugram in Haryana, where its corporate office RITES Bhawan is located.

q: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) was created mainly for:

options.A: Operating passenger trains on busy routes
options.B: Executing rail infrastructure projects on a fast-track basis through project-specific SPVs
options.C: Manufacturing rolling stock for Indian Railways

e: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited was incorporated in 2003 to execute rail infrastructure projects on a fast-track basis, largely through project-specific special purpose vehicles for capacity augmentation works.

q: The main function of the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) is:

options.A: Laying new railway lines in hilly areas
options.D: Commercial development of vacant railway land and air space for generating revenue

e: The Rail Land Development Authority is a statutory authority whose main job is the commercial development of vacant railway land and air space so that the Railways can earn non-tariff revenue from it.

q: The Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation (IRSDC) was set up for:

options.A: Redevelopment and modernisation of railway stations

e: The Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation was set up as a special purpose vehicle for the redevelopment and modernisation of railway stations on a commercial, self-sustainable model.

q: The Indian Railways Organisation for Alternate Fuels (IROAF), which was closed with effect from 07.09.2021, was concerned with:

options.A: Import of crude oil for diesel locomotives
options.B: Fixing the price of diesel purchased by Railways
options.C: Promoting the use of alternative and green fuels such as biodiesel and CNG in locomotives
options.D: Supply of coal to thermal power plants

e: IROAF worked on promoting alternative and green fuels such as biodiesel and CNG in locomotives, so as to cut diesel consumption and emissions. It was closed with effect from 07.09.2021 and its work was transferred to Northern Railway and the Railway Board. (Source: Railway Board order dated 07.09.2021; effective 07.09.2021).

q: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS) functions as:

options.A: A statutory corporation set up under the Railways Act
options.B: An autonomous society under the Ministry of Railways for information technology services
options.C: A division of the Railway Board Secretariat
options.D: A private software company on contract with Railways

e: The Centre for Railway Information Systems is an autonomous society registered under the Ministry of Railways; it designs, develops and maintains the information technology systems of Indian Railways.

q: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) has been set up as:

options.A: A special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways to plan, build and operate the dedicated freight corridors
options.B: A cooperative society of freight customers
options.C: A division of the Container Corporation of India
options.D: A joint venture of State Governments

e: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited is a special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways created to plan, construct, maintain and operate the dedicated freight corridors.

q: 'RailWire', the retail broadband service provided in association with local partners across India, is a brand of:
e: RailWire is the retail broadband brand of RailTel Corporation of India Limited, delivered at stations and in homes in association with local cable and access network partners.

q: Under its leasing model, the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) finances the acquisition of assets which are then leased to Indian Railways. These assets are mainly:

options.B: Rolling stock such as locomotives, coaches and wagons

e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation raises funds from the market and finances acquisition of rolling stock - locomotives, coaches and wagons - which is then leased to Indian Railways.

q: The inland container terminals of CONCOR, located away from the sea ports, are popularly known as:
e: CONCOR's inland container depots, set up away from sea ports for customs clearance and container handling close to trade centres, are popularly called dry ports.

q: Besides research and development, the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) is mainly responsible for:

options.B: Operating inspection trains on all zones
options.C: Framing standards and specifications for the designs and materials used on Indian Railways
options.D: Auditing the accounts of zonal railways

e: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation at Lucknow, besides research and development, frames the standards, codes and specifications for designs and materials adopted across Indian Railways.

q: IRCON International Limited is well known for undertaking:

options.A: Only maintenance work in railway workshops
options.B: Turnkey railway and infrastructure construction projects, including projects in foreign countries
options.D: Only supply of uniforms to railway staff

e: IRCON is known for executing turnkey railway and infrastructure construction projects on a turnkey basis, including large railway projects in foreign countries.

q: The Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi is a production unit engaged mainly in the manufacture of:
e: Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi is a production unit of Indian Railways engaged mainly in the manufacture of locomotives, earlier diesel and now largely electric locomotives.

q: The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala is engaged mainly in the manufacture of:
e: The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala in Punjab is a production unit whose main work is the manufacture of passenger coaches, including LHB coaches.

q: The Integral Coach Factory at Chennai is best known for the manufacture of:

options.D: Passenger coaches, including self-propelled train sets

e: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur, Chennai, is best known for building passenger coaches, including the self-propelled Vande Bharat train sets.

q: The Patiala Locomotive Works at Patiala is mainly engaged in:

options.B: Remanufacturing, modernisation and overhaul of diesel locomotives and their components

e: Patiala Locomotive Works at Patiala, earlier the Diesel Modernisation Works, is mainly engaged in remanufacturing, modernisation and overhaul of diesel locomotives and their components.

q: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela in Bihar mainly manufactures:

options.A: Cast wheels for locomotives, coaches and wagons

e: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela in Saran district of Bihar mainly manufactures cast wheels used in locomotives, coaches and wagons of Indian Railways.

q: The electric locomotive factory at Madhepura in Bihar has been set up as a joint venture of Indian Railways with:
e: The electric locomotive factory at Madhepura in Bihar is a joint venture of Indian Railways with Alstom, set up to build high-power 12000 HP electric freight locomotives.

q: The East Coast Railway, with headquarters at Bhubaneswar, became operational in the year:
e: East Coast Railway, headquartered at Bhubaneswar, was among the new zones announced in 1996 but became fully operational as a zone in 2003.

q: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur, Chennai, was inaugurated in the year:
e: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur, Chennai, was inaugurated in 1955 and began production of passenger coach shells in that year.

q: The Northeast Frontier Railway primarily serves the region of:
e: The Northeast Frontier Railway, headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati, primarily serves the north-eastern region of India along with parts of north Bengal and Bihar.

q: The Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi (earlier Diesel Locomotive Works) was set up in the year:
e: Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi, earlier called Diesel Locomotive Works, was set up in 1961 in collaboration with ALCO of the USA for making diesel locomotives.

q: The Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is located in which district of West Bengal?
e: Chittaranjan, where the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is situated, lies in Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'PMS', used for booking and tracking of parcels, stands for:
e: PMS in Indian Railways stands for Parcel Management System, the computer application used for booking, loading and tracking of parcels and for calculating charges like demurrage and wharfage.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'WISE', used in railway workshops, stands for:
e: WISE stands for Workshop Information System, the management information system implemented in major railway workshops for monitoring repair and overhaul work on rolling stock.

q: In Indian Railways, the module 'COIS' of the coaching information system stands for:
e: COIS stands for Coaching Operations Information System, the ICMS module that records operations of coaches, rakes and passenger locomotives and supports punctuality monitoring.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'COA', used by train controllers for charting of trains, stands for:
e: COA stands for Control Office Application, the system used by train controllers in divisional control offices for charting train movements and recording train running information.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'AIMS', used for accounts and payroll related work, stands for:
e: AIMS stands for Accounting Information Management System, the web-based application of the Accounts Department that handles accounting and payroll related work, earlier known as IPAS.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'TAMS', used in the Traffic Accounts offices, stands for:
e: TAMS stands for Traffic Accounts Management System, used in Traffic Accounts offices for checking and accounting of passenger, goods and other coaching earnings.

q: In Indian Railways, the stores computer application 'iMMS' stands for:
e: iMMS stands for Integrated Material Management System, the stores application of Indian Railways covering procurement, stocking and issue of materials.

q: In Indian Railways, the portal 'ROAMS', which gives a consolidated view of rolling stock assets, stands for:

options.A: Railway Operations and Asset Monitoring Service
options.B: Rolling Stock Operations and Management System

e: ROAMS stands for Rolling Asset Management System, the common web portal that gives managers a consolidated view of rolling stock assets, integrating systems like WISE, CMM and FMM.

q: In Indian Railways, the health scheme 'RELHS' for retired employees stands for:
e: RELHS stands for Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme, the scheme under which retired railway employees get medical facilities on making a contribution.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'RPF' stands for:
e: RPF stands for Railway Protection Force, the security force of Indian Railways responsible for protection of railway property, passenger areas and passengers.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'ARMV', a train kept ready for medical relief at accident sites, stands for:
e: ARMV stands for Accident Relief Medical Van, a special train kept in readiness with medical equipment and staff for relief work at accident sites.

q: The National Rail Plan 2030 mainly seeks to develop a 'future ready' railway system by:

options.A: Creating rail capacity ahead of the growing demand
options.B: Reducing the number of passenger trains
options.C: Handing over all freight traffic to the road sector
options.D: Closing down uneconomic branch lines only

e: The National Rail Plan 2030 aims to create rail capacity ahead of growing demand, so that a future ready railway system can raise the modal share of rail freight.

q: Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, the development of stations is to be carried out:

options.A: Only by demolishing and rebuilding every station building
options.B: Only during the year of launch of the scheme
options.C: Without any master plan, as and when funds permit
options.D: On a long-term basis through master plans, implemented in phases

e: Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, stations are developed on a long-term basis through master plans prepared for each station and implemented in phases.

q: The Vande Bharat Express trains are distinguished by the fact that they are:

options.A: Hauled by two separate locomotives at all times
options.B: Self-propelled train sets with distributed traction and no separate locomotive
options.C: Run only with steam locomotives on heritage routes
options.D: Composed only of unreserved general coaches

e: Vande Bharat Express trains are self-propelled train sets with distributed power and traction motors in coaches, so they run without a separate locomotive.

q: The 'Kavach' automatic train protection system of Indian Railways has been developed by:

options.B: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation, in collaboration with Indian industry

e: Kavach, the indigenous automatic train protection system, has been developed by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation in collaboration with Indian industry partners.

q: The digital platform for the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan has been developed by:

options.A: BISAG-N (Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics)
options.B: The Centre for Railway Information Systems
options.D: The Indian Space Research Organisation alone

e: The digital GIS-based platform for the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan has been developed by BISAG-N, the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics.

q: The Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project is significant mainly because it provides:

options.A: A rail line exclusively for freight traffic in the plains
options.B: A metro service within Srinagar city
options.C: A tourist-only narrow gauge line in Kashmir
options.D: All-weather rail connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of India

e: The Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link project gives the Kashmir Valley all-weather rail connectivity with the rest of India, ending its dependence only on road and air links.

q: The dedicated freight corridors are being built mainly to:

options.A: Run suburban trains between metropolitan cities
options.B: Carry freight trains on separate tracks, decongesting the busy passenger routes and raising freight speeds
options.C: Replace all existing broad gauge lines
options.D: Carry only parcel traffic of the postal department

e: The dedicated freight corridors carry freight trains on separate dedicated tracks, which decongests the saturated passenger routes and raises the average speed of goods trains.

q: Before the Hubballi platform became the longest in the world, the record for the world's longest railway platform was held by:
e: Before the Hubballi platform took the record, the platform at Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh was recognised as the longest railway platform in the world.

q: The Gandhinagar Capital railway station in Gujarat is notable as the first station in India to have:

options.A: A helipad on its roof for passengers
options.B: A platform made entirely of glass
options.C: A five-star hotel built above the station premises
options.D: A station building shaped like a train

e: Gandhinagar Capital station in Gujarat is the first station in India to have a five-star hotel built above the station premises as part of its redevelopment.

q: The first service of the upgraded Vande Bharat 2.0 train was introduced in 2022 on the route between:
e: The first service of the upgraded Vande Bharat 2.0 version was flagged off in 2022 between Gandhinagar Capital and Mumbai Central.

q: The book 'The Jungle Book' was written by:
e: The Jungle Book, the famous collection of stories featuring Mowgli, was written by Rudyard Kipling, the India-born Nobel laureate.

q: The novel 'Pride and Prejudice' was written by:
e: Pride and Prejudice, the classic novel of manners centred on Elizabeth Bennet, was written by the English novelist Jane Austen.

q: The novel 'Untouchable' was written by:
e: Untouchable, the novel depicting a day in the life of the sweeper Bakha, was written by Mulk Raj Anand, a pioneer of the Indian English novel.

q: The Booker Prize-winning novel 'Midnight's Children' was written by:
e: Midnight's Children, which won the Booker Prize in 1981, was written by Salman Rushdie and follows Saleem Sinai, born at the moment of India's independence.

q: The novel 'The White Tiger', which won the Booker Prize in 2008, was written by:
e: The White Tiger, the debut novel of Aravind Adiga narrated by driver Balram Halwai, won the Booker Prize in 2008.
